title: A Constrained, Data-Driven Budgeting Framework Integrating Macro Demand Forecasting and Marketing Response Modeling
authors: Lu, Y.; Zhou, H.; Zhang, Y.
venue: Journal of Technology Informatics and Engineering
tldr: An end-to-end framework integrates macro demand forecasting, marketing response modeling, and constrained optimization to allocate budgets under accounting constraints and demand uncertainty.
problem_and_motivation: Budgeting in FP&A must combine heterogeneous signals, nonlinear marketing returns, and accounting constraints into an auditable decision process. Existing approaches often treat components in isolation, lacking a coherent pipeline that links forecasts, response curves, and constraints under uncertainty. A reproducible, constraint-aware framework is needed to produce defensible budget recommendations.
approach: Quarterly PCE components from FRED (durables, nondurables, services) are used as a macro demand proxy in a rolling backtest from 2018Q1 to 2025Q3.
Demand is forecast using seasonal naïve, SARIMAX, gradient boosting, and a multivariate VAR model, with RMSE and MAPE as evaluation metrics.
Marketing response is estimated from the Advertising dataset using linear models, gradient boosting, and a Hill saturation function with 5-fold cross-validation.
Financial constraints—gross margin, SG&A ratio, and operating cash-flow coverage—are calibrated from Apple Inc.'s FY2025 Form 10-K.
A constrained portfolio optimization problem is solved via grid search over allocation shares and budget utilization, evaluated with 500 Monte Carlo scenarios.
Risk aversion is modeled through a mean-risk objective, and sensitivity analyses examine the impact of the marketing cap ratio and effectiveness normalization.
findings: Multivariate VAR improves aggregate demand accuracy with a MAPE of approximately 2.85%.
num: The Hill model achieves a cross-validated RMSE of 1.449 on the Advertising dataset.
The estimated coefficient for newspaper spend in the Hill model is effectively zero, indicating negligible incremental sales.
num: The risk-neutral optimizer selects a spend level of approximately 0.97% of revenue, below the 1.5% SG&A cap.
num: The optimal allocation is approximately 25% TV and 75% radio across all macro scenarios.
num: Spending at the deterministic cap would violate the SG&A constraint in roughly 40% of revenue realizations.
Higher risk aversion reduces budget utilization, trading off mean profit for lower volatility.
Optimal spend remains stable across marketing cap ratios above 1.5%, as diminishing returns bind before the cap.
When marketing effectiveness normalization is high (5% lift), the risk-neutral optimizer spends the full cap, reducing SG&A satisfaction to about 60%.
Sensitivity analyses show that optimal spend is more sensitive to response-curve assumptions than to cap-level debates.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: The paper contributes a modular, auditable pipeline that integrates macro demand forecasting, marketing response modeling, and constraint-aware optimization into a single budgeting framework. It provides empirical comparisons of forecasting models on public PCE data, demonstrating that multivariate VAR improves aggregate accuracy. It introduces a Hill saturation model for marketing response and calibrates financial constraints from real SEC filings, showing how optimization under uncertainty yields budgets below deterministic caps. The framework emphasizes reproducibility and governance through public data and explicit constraint documentation.
directly_justifies: Multivariate VAR improves total-demand accuracy with ≈2.85% MAPE.
Nonlinear response curves indicate strong diminishing returns and negligible incremental value for newspaper spend.
Budgets that meet a ratio-based cap under point forecasts may violate constraints under realistic demand uncertainty.
The optimizer selects a spend level below the cap, providing a buffer against revenue downside.
Risk aversion reduces budget utilization, trading off mean profit for lower volatility.
limits: Data sources are not internally consistent; PCE macro data and the Advertising dataset are from different contexts and normalized for demonstration.
Marketing response is treated as contemporaneous, omitting adstock/carryover effects common in real MMM applications.
The framework uses a stable market share assumption to map macro demand to firm revenue, which may not hold in practice.
The constraint calibration uses Apple Inc. data as a reference; in practice, firms would use internal audited statements.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: The topic taxonomy was systematically scanned across all domains. Domains 6.A, 6.B, 7.B, 7.C, 7.D were flagged as highly relevant due to the paper's core contribution on predictive modeling and constrained optimization for budget allocation. Domains 3.A, 12.A, 12.B, 14.A were flagged as medium or contextual relevance because the paper uses categorization, evaluation, and public data as supporting mechanisms. Domains related to Filipino demographics (1.A, 1.B, 1.C), culturally specific practices (2.A, 2.B, 2.C, 2.D), mobile-first design (9.A, 9.B, 9.C), privacy (10.A, 10.B, 10.C), engagement (11.A, 11.B), savings/debt management (13.A, 13.B, 13.C), and deployment (14.B, 14.C) were considered and rejected because the paper is a generic methodological framework for FP&A budgeting without cultural, demographic, mobile, privacy, engagement, or deployment-specific focus. The overall topical coverage centers on algorithmic budget recommendation under constraints, with supporting methodological evaluation.

limitations: Data sources are not internally consistent; PCE macro data and the Advertising dataset are from different contexts. [unacknowledged]
Marketing response is treated as contemporaneous, omitting adstock/carryover effects. [unacknowledged]
The stable market share assumption for linking macro demand to firm revenue may not hold in practice. [unacknowledged]
The normalization used to map advertising sales units to revenue dollars is a stylized approximation and should not be interpreted as true marketing ROI.
The use of latest-vintage FRED data overstates performance compared with strict real-time evaluation. [unacknowledged]
Alignment between calendar-quarter PCE data and fiscal-quarter corporate financials is abstracted away.
